entries.name: plotly.express.Constant
entries.summary: Objects of this class can be passed to Plotly Express functions that expect column identifiers or list-like objects to indicate that this attribute should take on a constant value. An optional label can be provided.

entries.name: plotly.express.IdentityMap
entries.summary: `dict`-like object which acts as if the value for any key is the key itself. Objects of this class can be passed in to arguments like `color_discrete_map` to use the provided data values as colors, rather than mapping them to colors cycled from `color_discrete_sequence`. This works for any `_map` argument to Plotly Express functions, such as `line_dash_map` and `symbol_map`.

entries.name: plotly.express.Range
entries.summary: Objects of this class can be passed to Plotly Express functions that expect column identifiers or list-like objects to indicate that this attribute should be mapped onto integers starting at 0. An optional label can be provided.

entries.name: plotly.express.area
entries.summary: In a stacked area plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a vertex of a polyline mark in 2D space. The area between successive polylines is filled.

entries.name: plotly.express.bar
entries.summary: In a bar plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a rectangular mark.

entries.name: plotly.express.bar_polar
entries.summary: In a polar bar plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a wedge mark in polar coordinates.

entries.name: plotly.express.box
entries.summary: In a box plot, rows of `data_frame` are grouped together into a box-and-whisker mark to visualize their distribution.

entries.name: plotly.express.choropleth
entries.summary: In a choropleth map, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a colored region mark on a map.

entries.name: plotly.express.choropleth_map
entries.summary: In a choropleth map, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a colored region on the map.

entries.name: plotly.express.density_contour
entries.summary: In a density contour plot, rows of `data_frame` are grouped together into contour marks to visualize the 2D distribution of an aggregate function `histfunc` (e.g. the count or sum) of the value `z`.

entries.name: plotly.express.density_heatmap
entries.summary: In a density heatmap, rows of `data_frame` are grouped together into colored rectangular tiles to visualize the 2D distribution of an aggregate function `histfunc` (e.g. the count or sum) of the value `z`.

entries.name: plotly.express.density_map
entries.summary: In a density map, each row of `data_frame` contributes to the intensity of the color of the region around the corresponding point on the map.

entries.name: plotly.express.ecdf
entries.summary: In a Empirical Cumulative Distribution Function (ECDF) plot, rows of `data_frame` are sorted by the value `x` (or `y` if `orientation` is `'h'`) and their cumulative count (or the cumulative sum of `y` if supplied and `orientation` is `h`) is drawn as a line.

entries.name: plotly.express.funnel
entries.summary: In a funnel plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a rectangular sector of a funnel.

entries.name: plotly.express.funnel_area
entries.summary: In a funnel area plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a trapezoidal sector of a funnel.

entries.name: plotly.express.get_trendline_results
entries.summary: Extracts fit statistics for trendlines (when applied to figures generated with the `trendline` argument set to `"ols"`).

entries.name: plotly.express.histogram
entries.summary: In a histogram, rows of `data_frame` are grouped together into a rectangular mark to visualize the 1D distribution of an aggregate function `histfunc` (e.g. the count or sum) of the value `y` (or `x` if `orientation` is `'h'`).

entries.name: plotly.express.icicle
entries.summary: An icicle plot represents hierarchial data with adjoined rectangular sectors that all cascade from root down to leaf in one direction.

entries.name: plotly.express.imshow
entries.summary: Display an image, i.e. data on a 2D regular raster.

entries.name: plotly.express.imshow_utils.rescale_intensity
entries.summary: Return image after stretching or shrinking its intensity levels.

entries.name: plotly.express.line
entries.summary: In a 2D line plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a vertex of a polyline mark in 2D space.

entries.name: plotly.express.line_3d
entries.summary: In a 3D line plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a vertex of a polyline mark in 3D space.

entries.name: plotly.express.line_geo

entries.name: plotly.express.line_map
entries.summary: In a line map, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a vertex of a polyline mark on the map.

entries.name: plotly.express.line_polar
entries.summary: In a polar line plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a vertex of a polyline mark in polar coordinates.

entries.name: plotly.express.line_ternary
entries.summary: In a ternary line plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a vertex of a polyline mark in ternary coordinates.

entries.name: plotly.express.parallel_categories
entries.summary: In a parallel categories (or parallel sets) plot, each row of `data_frame` is grouped with other rows that share the same values of `dimensions` and then plotted as a polyline mark through a set of parallel axes, one for each of the `dimensions`.

entries.name: plotly.express.parallel_coordinates
entries.summary: In a parallel coordinates plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a polyline mark which traverses a set of parallel axes, one for each of the `dimensions`.

entries.name: plotly.express.pie
entries.summary: In a pie plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a sector of a pie.

entries.name: plotly.express.scatter
entries.summary: In a scatter plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a symbol mark in 2D space.

entries.name: plotly.express.scatter_3d
entries.summary: In a 3D scatter plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a symbol mark in 3D space.

entries.name: plotly.express.scatter_geo
entries.summary: In a geographic scatter plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a symbol mark on a map.

entries.name: plotly.express.scatter_map
entries.summary: In a scatter map, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a symbol mark on the map.

entries.name: plotly.express.scatter_matrix
entries.summary: In a scatter plot matrix (or SPLOM), each row of `data_frame` is represented by a multiple symbol marks, one in each cell of a grid of 2D scatter plots, which plot each pair of `dimensions` against each other.

entries.name: plotly.express.scatter_polar
entries.summary: In a polar scatter plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a symbol mark in polar coordinates.

entries.name: plotly.express.scatter_ternary
entries.summary: In a ternary scatter plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented by a symbol mark in ternary coordinates.

entries.name: plotly.express.strip
entries.summary: In a strip plot each row of `data_frame` is represented as a jittered mark within categories.

entries.name: plotly.express.sunburst
entries.summary: A sunburst plot represents hierarchial data as sectors laid out over several levels of concentric rings.

entries.name: plotly.express.timeline
entries.summary: In a timeline plot, each row of `data_frame` is represented as a rectangular mark on an x axis of type `date`, spanning from `x_start` to `x_end`.

entries.name: plotly.express.treemap
entries.summary: A treemap plot represents hierarchial data as nested rectangular sectors.

entries.name: plotly.shapeannotation.axis_spanning_shape_annotation
entries.summary: annotation: a go.layout.Annotation object, a dict describing an annotation, or None shape_type: one of 'vline', 'hline', 'vrect', 'hrect' and determines how the x, y, xanchor, and yanchor values are set. shape_args: the parameters used to draw the shape, which are used to place the annotation kwargs:     a dictionary that was the kwargs of a _process_multiple_axis_spanning_shapes spanning shapes call. Items in this dict whose keys start with 'annotation_' will be extracted and the keys with the 'annotation_' part stripped off will be used to assign properties of the new annotation.
